title: SoundWire-style two-wire audio bus interface (manager or peripheral) with control commands and one data port each way

regs.name: CFG
regs.desc: Role, frame shape, device number, data columns

fields.desc: 1 = manager (drives CLOCK and the control word)
manager: bit time - 1 in PCLK (11 or more)
transmit column (0 or past the last column = off)
receive column (0 or past the last column = off)
peripheral: status sent in its PING slot

regs.name: CMD
regs.desc: Manager: command for the next frame; writing CMD commits it

regs.name: RSP
regs.desc: Manager: response to a command; reading RSP frees it

fdesc.rsp_rdata: data bits of the frame (READ data, WRITE data echoed)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Transmit sample for the data port; writing TX commits it for the next frame

fdesc.tx_data: sample, MSB first in rows 0..31 of the column

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received sample from the data port; reading RX frees it

fields.desc: manager: status bits of the last PING, device 1 in [15:14]

irqs.name: LOST_SYNC
irqs.desc: peripheral: two bad frames in a row, the lock is dropped

irqs.name: PAR_ERR
irqs.desc: peripheral: a command to this device failed the parity check (answered with NAK)

irqs.name: TX_UNDERRUN
irqs.desc: the transmit column found no sample (zeros sent)

notes: sw_clk_o / sw_clk_oe / sw_clk_i and sw_dat_o / sw_dat_oe / sw_dat_i are the bus pins (CLOCK from the manager; DATA multi-drop with a bus keeper); all pass through unchanged.
reg_we / reg_re / reg_addr / reg_wdata and reg_rdata are the peripheral's register interface; they pass through unchanged (reg_rdata is read combinationally from reg_addr).
